nodes.statement: The product is currently defined as 'secretome retaining EVs' versus a purified small‑EV drug substance; this distinction is unresolved and blocks product definition and CMC decisions.

If a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (intact-EV capture, particle counts, detergent/protease sensitivity, density correlation) is observed, then the preparation can be classified as an EV-enriched small‑EV preparation rather than mainly non‑vesicular secretome.

If no membrane-protected, particle-associated signature is observed and marker signal tracks with bulk soluble protein and is insensitive to membrane disruption, then the preparation is indistinguishable from an unpurified secretome with co-isolated non‑vesicular components.
Classifying the drug‑substance fractionation state enables targeted CMC actions: orthogonal QC panel, potency assay development, and relevant scale-up comparability testing (MISEV2023 guidance).

nodes.statement: An orthogonally defined intact-EV signature (capture-positive, particle-peak co-localization, detergent/protease-sensitive) identifies a membrane-protected fraction in the drug substance.

If an administered preparation contains the orthogonal intact-EV signature and intact-EV exposure in the nasal→CSF/olfactory mucosa compartment is demonstrable in vivo, then downstream CNS immune cells (microglia-like cells) will show a reproducible ex vivo modulation measurable in a standardized cytokine readout.

If the preparation lacks the intact-EV signature or the captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, then the ex vivo CNS readout will be absent or qualitatively different, showing that bulk particle counts alone do not predict the assay outcome.

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Integrated protocol: (A) characterize administered materials in vitro with orthogonal intact-EV workflow (density fractionation + particle counts + immuno-capture + detergent/protease protection); (B) intranasal administration to rodents with short post-dose interval (predefined, brief window) followed by collection of nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue; (C) orthogonal verification of intact-EV exposure in collected fluids/tissues (capture and particle counts); (D) prepare ex vivo tissue or isolated microglia-like cells from harvested tissue, apply standardized inflammatory challenge (e.g., LPS) and measure cytokine release with and without co-incubation with eluates from captured fractions; (E) compare cytokine responses across arms.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Four-arm comparison from the same conditioned-medium lot: (1) intact-EV-enriched preparation (capture-positive), (2) secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium (capture profile to be determined), (3) intact-EV-enriched material treated with detergent + protease prior to administration (membrane-disrupted), (4) particle-count-matched but capture-depleted preparation (if achievable).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in the ex vivo assay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions. In-assay viability/assay controls for tissue health.

nodes.statement: Donor-MSC senescence state (operationalized by passage number and p16/p21 expression) determines features of the released particle population (membrane integrity, surface-marker display, particle:protein ratio).

These senescence-linked particle features produce a distinct orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature: capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive versus marker signal that tracks with bulk soluble protein and is detergent-insensitive.

Materials with the senescence-favorable intact-EV signature are more likely to produce short-interval in vivo evidence of intact-EV presence in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after intranasal dosing than materials from senescent MSC sources.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Does the donor MSC senescence state (early-passage, low p16/p21 expression versus late-passage, high p16/p21 expression) causally alter (A) the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) and (B) short-interval nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa intact-EV detection after matched intranasal dosing of conditioned-medium-derived preparations?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow: (1) density-gradient fractionation with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture + detection of EV surface markers on intact fractions; (3) protease and RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) measure total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction. For in vivo arm: perform orthogonal capture and particle count on short-interval collected lavage/CSF/tissues.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matched conditioned-medium-derived preparations from the same donor source processed identically: early-passage (low p16/p21) versus late-passage (high p16/p21); within each, compare enriched small-EV preparation and secretome-retaining preparation. Include detergent/protease-disrupted aliquots as membrane-disruption controls.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only, vehicle-only, and detergent-disrupted capture material. Positive controls: commercially available characterized small EVs (if available) and a lab-validated non-senescent MSC small-EV preparation.

minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met, the hypothesis that source-cell senescence state deterministically controls intact-EV analytical signature and short-interval intranasal recoverability is falsified; the program should deprioritize senescence as a gating source-cell specification and investigate alternative source or process variables (donor genetics, media, purification artifacts) as drivers of observed variability.

nodes.statement: A scalable fractionation workflow (TFF → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion) can produce a size- and density-bounded fraction with a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity).

The concentrated conditioned-medium (secretome-retaining) processed only by TFF concentration lacks the co-localized capture-positive particle peak and shows marker signal that is largely detergent/protease-insensitive, consistent with non-vesicular co-isolates.

If n1 is true and yields are manufacturable, the bounded small-EV fraction can serve as a reproducible drug-substance definition to support orthogonal QC and potency assay development (inference; uncertainty noted).

nodes.statement: Downstream processing exposures (number of freeze-thaw cycles and contact with candidate formulation buffers) can alter membrane integrity, surface-marker accessibility, and particle:protein characteristics of MSC-conditioned-medium-derived material.

If membrane integrity and surface-marker display are lost, the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) will be abolished while bulk particle counts may remain similar.

Preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature through defined downstream-process conditions enables use of that signature as a process gate for drug-substance definition and supports development of potency-linked assays.

nodes.statement: TFF concentration operating parameters (transmembrane pressure, flux, cumulative processed volume per membrane) can mechanically or shear-damage EV membranes or otherwise alter surface-marker accessibility without necessarily changing bulk particle counts.

Loss of membrane integrity or marker accessibility will abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) while particle counters may report similar counts due to non-membrane particle debris.

Demonstrating a reproducible, parameter-linked loss of orthogonal signature across scale-relevant TFF conditions distinguishes true scale effects from analytical noise and enables definition of an operational TFF envelope as a manufacturing control.

nodes.statement: If a membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction contains a reproducible multi-omic cargo fingerprint across independent production lots, then that fingerprint can serve as a lot-consistency metric independent of an assigned single active molecule.

If candidate fingerprint elements (protected miRNAs, detergent-sensitive protein markers, lipid-class ratios) are absent or variable across lots or are present in secretome-retaining fractions equivalently, then the preparation lacks an EV-associated cargo consistency signal and cannot be gated as an EV-consistent drug substance without additional fractionation or source controls.

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV capture workflow with density fractionation and particle counting to identify particle-peak fractions followed by: (1) protected-cargo small-RNA profiling (targeted panel/seq) on capture-positive fractions ± detergent/protease, (2) targeted proteomics for candidate EV luminal/surface proteins on protected material ± protease, (3) targeted lipidomics of particle-peak fractions, and (4) computation of cross-lot fingerprint similarity metrics (hierarchical clustering and pairwise similarity indices).

Include on-fraction detergent+protease/RNase-treated aliquots to test membrane protection. Include positive control small EV prep (commercial or lab-validated) and negative buffer-only controls.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted capture eluates; Positive controls: characterized small EV preparation processed in parallel; spike-in synthetic miRNA/protein/lipid standards to monitor recovery.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed ex vivo modulation could result from soluble co-isolates that reach CNS compartments independently of intact EVs or from administration/dosing differences rather than intact-EV presence.
edges.missing_experiment: Orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridging experiment comparing capture-positive, membrane-intact material versus membrane-disrupted and capture-depleted controls with short-interval tissue sampling.
edges.uncertainty: High: rodent efficacy and MISEV support the need for orthogonal linkage but do not demonstrate an in vivo→ex vivo causal bridge; inference that intact-EV exposure is necessary for short-interval ex vivo modulation requires empirical testing.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect in vivo exposure could arise from assay insensitivity or labeling artifacts rather than absence of intact EVs.
edges.missing_experiment: A matched intact-EV verification assay in short-interval in vivo samples concurrent with ex vivo functional readout.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: limited large-animal biodistribution after intranasal dosing suggests delivery barriers that could confound potency linkage, but the result may reflect formulation/labeling differences.

nodes.statement: An orthogonally defined intact-EV signature (capture-positive, particle-peak co-localization, detergent/protease-sensitive) identifies a membrane-protected EV fraction in conditioned medium.

If an administered preparation contains the orthogonal intact-EV signature and intact-EV exposure in nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa compartments is verifiable in vivo, then a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation will be observed from tissue-derived microglia-like cells.

If the administered preparation lacks the intact-EV signature, or the captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, then the short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation will be absent or qualitatively different.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Does in vivo short-interval nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa exposure of an orthogonally verified, membrane-protected, capture-positive EV fraction causally enable a reproducible ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation that is lost when the same material is membrane-disrupted or capture-depleted?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Integrated protocol: (A) characterize administered materials in vitro with orthogonal intact-EV workflow (density fractionation + particle counts + immuno-capture + detergent/protease protection); (B) intranasal administration to rodents with short post-dose interval followed by collection of nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue; (C) orthogonal verification of intact-EV exposure in collected fluids/tissues (capture and particle counts); (D) prepare ex vivo tissue-derived microglia-like cells, apply standardized inflammatory challenge (LPS) and measure cytokine release with and without co-incubation with captured-fraction eluates; (E) compare cytokine responses across arms.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Four-arm comparison from the same conditioned-medium lot: (1) intact-EV-enriched preparation (capture-positive), (2) secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining), (3) intact-EV-enriched material treated with detergent + protease prior to administration (membrane-disrupted), (4) particle-count-matched but capture-depleted preparation (if achievable).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in the ex vivo assay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions. In-assay viability/assay controls for tissue health.
dependencies: Availability of sufficient conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank and passage range
Validated immuno-capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation sensitivity for low-biomass lavage/CSF samples
Animal protocol approvals for short-interval tissue/fluid collection
Laboratory capability to run both orthogonal capture and ex vivo inflammatory assays
minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible linkage between in vivo orthogonal intact-EV verification and the ex vivo cytokine readout across replicates, or particle-count-matched capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent ex vivo effects, indicating activity is not intact-EV-associated.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met, treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome with respect to the tested short-term ex vivo inflammatory readout; revise product-definition toward secretome-centric strategy and deprioritize EV-specific potency attribute.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: An intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected fraction (verified by capture + detergent/protease sensitivity and particle-peak co-localization) is necessary for a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation following intranasal administration; particle-count-matched but capture-negative or membrane-disrupted material will not produce the same ex vivo modulation.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.primary_readout: Magnitude and reproducibility of ex vivo cytokine modulation (e.g., reduction in LPS-induced IL-6/TNF-α) from tissue-derived microglia-like cells correlated with in vivo orthogonal evidence of intact-EV exposure (presence of capture-positive signal and particle co-localization in lavage/CSF/tissue).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.question: Can an orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridge show that only capture-positive, membrane-protected material produces a reproducible short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal administration, independent of bulk particle counts?

Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions

Confirmation that captured material's activity is abolished by detergent + protease pre-treatment

Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium preps and animal cohorts)
minimum_discriminating_experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In multiple independent conditioned-medium lots and animal cohorts (n ≥ 3), only the arm where administered material is orthogonally verified as capture-positive and shows particle-peak co-localization produces a reproducible reduction in ex vivo inflammatory cytokine readout; this reduction is abolished when captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, and particle-count-matched capture-negative or secretome-retaining arms do not produce equivalent ex vivo modulation.

prior_hypotheses.proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, adopt a mechanism-linked potency gate: an intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity (co-localizing with particle peaks, capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive) that predicts a short-interval ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal administration and serves as a potency-linked product-identity attribute.

edges.missing_experiment: Program-specific co-fractionation with detergent/protease protection to confirm membrane association and rule out co-eluting non-vesicular sources.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends membrane-protection and orthogonal capture as distinguishing features but does not prescribe exact marker panels or thresholds.

edges.competing_explanation: Even if the surface-phenotype metric is measurable, it may not predict in vivo exposure differences (delivery barriers or species differences may dominate).
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo verification of capture-positive material in lavage/CSF/tissue to connect identity measurement with recoverable exposure.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: large-animal negative biodistribution after intranasal dosing increases the need for a rigorous identity gate, but does not prove that surface-phenotype preservation will enable cross-species delivery.

nodes.statement: Presence of immuno-capture-positive canonical EV surface markers on intact material that co-localize with particle-count peaks identifies a membrane-protected particle population distinct from soluble secretome co-isolates.

Detergent + protease/RNase sensitivity of capture-positive signal (loss after membrane disruption) distinguishes membrane-protected surface-marker display from marker signal arising from non-vesicular co-isolates.
Defining this orthogonal surface-phenotype metric enables a reproducible product-identity gate that is independent of bulk particle-counts and supports downstream QC and comparability workflows.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily design question: Which specific intact-EV surface-marker measurements (capture-positive signal on intact material, detergent/protease sensitivity, and co-localization with particle-peak fractions) constitute a reproducible product-identity metric that discriminates EV-enriched drug-substance candidates from secretome-retaining concentrates without implying potency?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal fraction-level workflow combining: (1) fractionation (iodixanol cushion or SEC) with particle-count per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture detection of canonical EV surface markers on intact fractions; (3) protease and RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.

Positive control: characterized small EV preparation processed in parallel.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples. Positive controls: characterized small EV prep and capture-reagent compatibility panels.

minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If the failure criteria are met, the hypothesis is falsified: the proposed intact-EV surface-marker phenotype cannot be used as a discriminating product-identity metric and the program should treat surface-marker readouts as insufficient for identity gating and prioritize alternative fractionation, assay development, or secretome-centric definitions.

edges.missing_experiment: Matrixed capture-reagent compatibility controls and detergent/protease protection checks for each excipient and device-exposure condition.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal analytics and notes processing sensitivity but does not quantify specific excipient or device thresholds.

edges.competing_explanation: In vitro bioactivity could be mediated by soluble factors that survive or are unaffected by excipients, so bioactivity preservation might not track with membrane-protection.
edges.missing_experiment: Parallel identity and protected-bioactivity readouts after formulation/device exposures.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: rodent functional observations exist but do not establish that preserved membrane protection or identity metrics are required for activity; linkage must be tested.

edges.competing_explanation: Delivery failures in large animals may reflect administration route or species-specific clearance independent of formulation/device compatibility.

edges.uncertainty: High: large-animal nasal delivery uncertainty increases priority of compatibility testing, but does not identify which excipients or device parameters are causal for detectability loss.

nodes.statement: Contact with specific nasal formulation excipient classes (ionic strength extremes, non-ionic surfactants, chelators) or passage through delivery-device geometries that create shear can alter EV membrane integrity or surface-marker accessibility without changing bulk particle counts.

Loss of membrane integrity or mask­ing of surface epitopes will abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) while particle counters report limited change.

If a candidate formulation/device condition preserves the orthogonal intact-EV signature, the same condition will also preserve a membrane-protected in vitro neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity (or conversely, loss of the signature will correlate with loss of membrane-protected bioactivity).

Defining formulation/device compatibility by preservation of both the orthogonal identity signature and membrane-protected bioactivity enables a non-assumptive, functional compatibility gate suitable for CMC and comparability decisions.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Which specific nasal vehicle excipient classes and device shear exposures preserve an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) and a matched in vitro membrane-protected anti-inflammatory bioactivity, versus those that abolish both signatures despite similar bulk particle counts?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Parallel orthogonal workflows: (1) density/size fractionation with particle counting per fraction and immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture on intact fractions to assess co-localization; (2) protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material to test membrane protection; (3) apply matched fraction eluates to the in vitro neuroinflammation assay (LPS-challenged microglia readout) to test protected bioactivity; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratios per fraction; (5) capture-reagent buffer-compatibility panels to detect assay interference.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matrixed, paired comparisons per conditioned-medium lot: (A) no-exposure control (aliquot in baseline buffer, no device pass), versus (B...N) each formulation buffer condition ± device-shear exposure (low/mid/high). Include detergent/protease-disrupted aliquots as negative membrane-protection controls and capture-reagent compatibility controls (capture reagent incubated with formulation buffer alone).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV prep processed identically; assay positive control: dexamethasone in bioassay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer-only fractions. Capture-compatibility controls for each excipient condition.

minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If the failure criterion is met, the hypothesis is falsified for the tested excipient/device envelope: the program should not assume formulation/device compatibility preserves intact-EV identity or protected bioactivity, and must investigate alternative approaches (immediate capture/lyophilization, secretome-centric product definition, or alternative delivery routes).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: Specific formulation excipient classes and delivery-device shear exposures will either preserve or abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks + detergent/protease sensitivity) and a matched membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity; conditions that preserve both are compatible for intranasal use without assuming prior EV identity.

nodes.statement: Orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive surface-marker co-localization with particle peaks, detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal, protected-cargo fingerprint, and particle:protein ratio) operationally report membrane integrity and EV-associated cargo protection in the drug substance.

Storage and formulation exposures (temperature, time, freeze-thaw, excipient class, device-shear) that damage EV membranes or strip associated cargo will abolish or substantially alter these orthogonal signatures while bulk particle counts may be preserved.

If orthogonal signatures change reproducibly with defined exposures, then those signatures can be used as stability-indicating attributes to define acceptable storage/formulation envelopes and as comparability criteria during manufacturing scale-up.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily design question: Which orthogonal intact-EV analytical signals (surface-marker capture co-localized with particle peaks, detergent/protease protection, protected-cargo multi-omic fingerprint, and particle:protein ratio) are reliably lost or altered by clinically relevant storage and formulation exposures and therefore serve as stability-indicating attributes for SGL-001?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal stability workflow per condition: (1) fractionation (density or size) with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture on intact fractions and capture ELISA/bead readout for canonical surface markers; (3) detergent + protease/RNase protection testing on captured material; (4) protected-cargo profiling (targeted small-RNA panel ± detergent treatment; targeted proteomics ± protease); (5) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (6) capture-compatibility panels to detect assay interference.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matrixed within-lot paired comparisons: (A) no-exposure baseline control, versus matrixed conditions including defined storage temperatures (e.g., refrigerated, room temperature, elevated), durations (short/medium), 0/1/3 freeze-thaw cycles, each formulation excipient condition, and device-shear exposures. Include detergent/protease-disrupted aliquots and capture-compatibility buffer-only controls.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples; capture-compatibility controls (capture reagents incubated with formulation buffers alone). Positive controls: commercially available characterized small EV prep (if available) processed identically and spike-in synthetic standards for omic assays; in-bioassay positive anti-inflammatory control (e.g., dexamethasone) for downstream optional protected-bioactivity readout.
